summary: Trinity stops and turns on Neo after his remark, demanding to know what he said. Neo explains he had a deja vu: a black cat went past them and then another that looked just like it appeared, and he admits 'It might have been' the same cat. Trinity presses him about how alike they were, then looks to Morpheus, who listens quietly to the building's breathing. When Neo asks what is going on, Trinity explains that a déjà vu is typically a glitch in the Matrix that happens when 'they change something.' Both she and Morpheus then listen as the sound of helicopter blades grows ominously loud.

what_changes.before: Unaware of the significance of the repeated cat, treating it as 'Just had a little deja vu.'
what_changes.after: Told by Trinity that a deja vu is typically a glitch in the Matrix' that 'happens when they change something,' revealing the world is being altered.
what_changes.evidence: A deja vu is usually a glitch

what_changes.before: Alert and interrogating Neo about what he saw, still investigating the cat.
what_changes.after: Listening with Morpheus to the growing 'staccato BEAT of HELICOPTER BLADES' that 'GROWS ominously LOUD,' signalling approaching danger.
what_changes.evidence: She also listens as the staccato BEAT

event_hint.one_line: A deja vu reveals the Matrix is being changed, and helicopter blades signal an approaching raid on the building.

minds.wants: To confirm, in a split second, whether the déjà vu is a real glitch — and to convert that confirmation into a threat-assessment before the crew is caught exposed in the open stairwell.
minds.feels: A cold, fast surge of alarm. The word 'deja vu' has already stopped her dead (sc-091); now she is running the worst-case scenario — that the Matrix is being actively rewritten around them, meaning Agents are close. Her interrogation is not curiosity, it is triage.
minds.shows: A tight, controlled, almost clinical line of questioning ('How similar was it? Was it the identical feline?'). She keeps her voice flat and factual, then lets the explanation to Neo double as her own confirmation — before she goes still to listen for the helicopters.
minds.basis: Her face is 'tight' and she snaps 'What did you just say?' at a trivial remark; in sc-091 the those words freeze everyone in their place.' She presses for the degree of resemblance rather than accepting 'deja vu' as a figure of speech, then looks to Morpheus and listens. She frames the glitch as 'when they change something' — 'they' being the enemy.

believes_about.belief: That he is still too new and untrained to grasp what a déjà vu means — that she has to translate reality for him under fire.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is exactly the moment Neo begins to read the Matrix the way a freed mind does; her belief that he is only a passenger to be briefed will be disproven as the raid unfolds and he starts acting on instinct.

believes_about.belief: That in this instant Morpheus is doing what she is doing — listening for the same threat and will give the same read — so their wordless look settles the situation between them.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus is listening to something else entirely ('the RASPING breath of the old BUILDING'), a layer of the environment Trinity does not register; their agreement here is her assumption, not something the scene confirms.

minds.wants: First to brush off his slip as nothing, then — once he reads how seriously they take it — to get them to tell him what is actually happening.
minds.feels: A quick embarrassment at having said something 'stupid,' immediately overtaken by a jolt of recognition that this world operates by rules he does not yet know, and that his throwaway observation has just become significant. He is being pulled from civilian reflexes into operational reality.
minds.shows: A shrug of dismissal ('Nothing. Just had a little deja vu'), then a hedged, uncertain answer ('It might have been. I'm not sure'), then the direct, exposed question 'What is it?' — the moment he stops pretending and admits he is out of his depth.
minds.basis: He first denies ('Nothing'), then offers the cat detail, then hedges rather than commit, then explicitly asks 'What is it?' — a sequence that moves from deflection to admission of not knowing. His 'Whoa. Deja vu' in sc-091 was casual; here he is reading the adults' reactions and recalibrating.

believes_about.belief: That her intensity is disproportionate — that he has startled her over a harmless coincidence and she is overreacting.
believes_about.wrong_because: Her intensity is precisely calibrated to a real event: a glitch means the Agents are altering the simulation. His assumption that she is overreacting is the last civilian misreading he will make before the helicopters prove her right.

minds.wants: To gather the maximum information from the environment — not just the human explanation but the building itself — so he can locate the threat before it locates them.
minds.feels: A deep, unmoved stillness that is actually hyper-attentiveness. Where Trinity keys on the human-sign of the glitch, Morpheus is tuned to the physical substrate ('the RASPING breath of the old BUILDING'), reading the world at a layer beneath the others. There is no panic, only assessment.
minds.shows: Nothing outward: he listens 'quietly,' says nothing, offers no interpretation. He lets Trinity brief Neo while he does the work of listening — his silence is the most senior person in the room not needing to perform certainty.
minds.basis: While the other two exchange words, the text isolates him listening to the building's breath, and only after does Trinity's look toward him register. His silence here matches the Oracle's-event context in which he carries an unshakeable, private certainty about Neo.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is the one to be protected and guided toward his destiny, and that this protection is worth any risk to the crew — a conviction freshly reinforced by the Oracle.
believes_about.wrong_because: That private belief is what will soon force the choice the Oracle named (Neo's life or Morpheus's) and will lead directly to Morpheus's capture; the certainty that shields Neo does not shield Morpheus.

connects_back: Neo's casual 'Whoa. Deja vu' and the identical black cats in sc-091, which is the raw observation this scene interrogates.
The crew stopping dead at the word in sc-091 — Trinity's 'tight' face here is the continuation of that shared, trained alarm.
The Main Deck glitch ('Oh shit! Oh shit!') in sc-092 — the objective, external confirmation that a rewrite is in progress, which Trinity and Morpheus are hearing the consequences of.
The Oracle's prophecy (ev-021) and her instruction to keep the verdict secret, which sits under Morpheus's silence and Trinity's protective vigilance as they move toward the trap.
sets_up: The confirmation that a déjà vu signals 'they change something' makes the bricking-up of the windows and the building lockdown in ev-022 legible as a deliberate Agent action rather than a random event.
The growing helicopter blades establish the raid on the Hotel Lafayette in ev-022, including Mouse being left behind and the crew being trapped.
The crew being caught exposed in the open stairwell sets up the desperate escape and extraction in ev-023.
Morpheus's quiet, self-possessed certainty here feeds the Oracle-named choice between Neo's life and Morpheus's, which drives Morpheus's capture and the rescue in ev-024 through ev-027.
dramatic_function: It converts a small, eerie coincidence into the story's tripwire: the exposition of 'deja vu = a glitch when they change something' is delivered not as a lecture but as an in-progress threat diagnosis, so the audience learns the rules of the Matrix at the exact moment those rules begin to close around the characters — turning wonder into imminent danger.
